handoffPurpose: Capture the world-map placement fix and follow-up interaction performance pass after reports of map overlap, pan/zoom lag, and touch-effect hitches.
currentUserGoal: Move the world map out of the playing field and make pan, zoom, arrow-key movement, and on-touch feedback feel smoother on large fields.

workCompleted.summary: Moved the world map from the lower-left board area to the top-right floating UI rail beside the Skills/Quests command buttons, and hid it on phone-sized portrait views where it would compete with the board.
Kept pan and zoom layouts from re-laying static floating UI. Interaction layouts now update the world-map viewport marker and hover marker without redoing trigger-feed/map layout.
Deferred periodic full UI refresh while board layout, common-layer preview, common redraw, or map dragging is active, so decorative refresh work does not land in the middle of movement.
Stopped weather particle effects from being destroyed and recreated during ordinary weather layout; they now rebuild only when weather changes, quality changes, or viewport dimensions change.

Prewarmed common gameplay burst emitters shortly after startup and applied the existing ambient feedback budget to manual touches on large fields to reduce mid-play effect allocation and burst pressure.

verificationPerformed.result: Passed with only the existing LF-to-CRLF warning.
World map no longer overlaps the board; it sits in the top-right UI rail beside the command buttons.

knownIssuesOrDesignQuestions: Phone 1200-tile harness remains in viewport-live-tile mode and reports displayObjects around 884. It is spike-free in this pass, but a future mobile-specific object-count pass could reduce that pressure.
Large stress pages can still show a one-time initial layout/composite hotspot during startup. The repeatable complete phases and interaction checks are clean.
The world map is hidden below 760px wide and on mobile portrait. If a future design needs a phone minimap, it should probably be a modal or compact toggle rather than a floating board overlay.
recommendedNextSteps: Play manually on the desktop for feel, especially repeated arrow-key panning and mouse-wheel zooming.
If phone display-object pressure becomes visible, investigate reducing viewport-live tile object parts or switching compact large fields to a more batch-like path.
Consider adding a tiny perf harness phase that repeats multiple arrow-key pans, since the current harness only samples one pan.
doNotRevert: Do not move the world map back into the board content area; it caused direct tile overlap.
Keep weather particle recreation guarded by viewport/weather/quality changes. Recreating particles during ordinary UI layout was a hidden hitch source.
Keep pan/zoom ancillary UI work marker-only unless static UI actually needs layout.
Keep burst emitter prewarming or replace it with another strategy that avoids first-touch emitter creation during gameplay.
